My best guess is that palpating the jugular venous pulse is the unnecessary step, since the JVP is assessed by inspection and palpation picks up the carotid instead. Positioning at about 30–45° with the head turned slightly away, and measuring height above the sternal angle (plus 5 cm for right atrial pressure), are standard parts of the exam. Without the answer options I can't be certain, so paste them and I'll give a definite answer.

CONFIDENCE: 45
